question.text: Which of the following best describes the portfolio manager's obligation regarding the Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC) document?

answer.text: MITC is an internal compliance note and is not shared with clients
Portfolio managers are required to provide clients with an MITC document in the standard format prescribed by SEBI/APMI
MITC is only required for clients who invest more than Rs. 5 crore in PMS
MITC is an optional disclosure that the portfolio manager may choose to provide

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI's framework for portfolio managers requires that clients be furnished with a Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC) document at the time of subscription, in a standard format prescribed jointly by SEBI and the industry association APMI. The MITC is designed to surface the most critical features of the PMS engagement — fees, risks, exit terms, conflicts — in a single concise document so the client can take an informed decision. Providing the MITC is a regulatory obligation, not a discretionary disclosure. The Trap: Treating MITC as an internal note ignores its client-disclosure purpose. Restricting it to clients above any specific investment size is not part of the regulatory requirement; the obligation applies generally to PMS clients. Calling it optional contradicts the prescriptive nature of the requirement. Note: The cited NISM Series XXI-B Portfolio Managers workbook (p.151) states that portfolio managers shall provide clients an MITC document in the standard format and references a May 2024 SEBI/APMI circular, but does not state an effective or mandated-from date such as Oct 1, 2024. The framing above is drawn from the workbook's obligation statement rather than from a specific calendar date.
